newsitem.title: USA: Norwest says loan quality little worse.
newsitem.headline: Norwest says loan quality little worse.

text.p: Norwest Corp, which on Monday reported an increase in third quarter earnings, said the quality of its consumer loans has not significantly deteriorated.
"Although there continues to be a national focus on consumer credit quality, Norwest's consumer credit quality has not experienced a noteworthy deterioration," the company said in a statement.
Credit card receivables past due over 30 days were 4.01 percent as of September 30, as compared with 3.87 percent at June 30 and 3.88 percent at year-end 1995, Norwest said.
Norwest Financial's consumer loan delinquencies over 60 days were 3.73 percent, up slightly from 3.59 percent at June 30 and 3.41 percent at December 31.
Norwest Mortgage's delinquencies over 30 days in the servicing portfolio were 5.5 percent at September 30, versus 4.9 and five percent at June 30 and December 31, respectively.

Norwest said it provided $105.9 million for credit losses in the third quarter, or 107 basis points of averages loans and leases on an annualized basis. This compares with $86.5 million, or 95 basis points, in the second quarter.
Consolidated non-income was $631.8 million in the third quarter, versus $483.7 million for the quarter last year and $641.9 million in the second quarter.

Venture Capital gains were $35.7 million in the third quarter compared with $65.5 million in the second quarter of 1996. As of September 30, Norwest Venture had a net unrealized appreciation in its investment portfolio of $256.8 million, the company said.
Norwest reported third quarter earnings of $0.76 per primary share versus $0.70 last year.
Its total assets were $78.4 billion versus $71.4 in third quarter 1995, net loans and leases were $39.1 billion compared with $35.7 billion and total deposits were $48.0 billion versus $39.7 billion.
